html:
SMTO-CTX-0052 — SMTO couldn't confirm where this image came from

GUID: daec263c-8560-5bb6-a194-5743b6c4c0f3
Slug: attachment-image-provenance
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • SMTO only lets the model look at pictures it can trace back to a file you attached or a page or screen it captured itself. This picture had no such record, so the model has not looked at it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the message box, select Add context and attach the original image or PDF file you want SMTO to look at. SMTO trusts pictures you attached yourself because it knows exactly where they came from.
  2. Send a message asking about that attached file, for example "Look at page 3 of the attached PDF". For a PDF, SMTO turns the page into a picture itself, which gives that picture a record it can check.
  3. Don't point SMTO at a picture only by its file name or a copy saved somewhere else. A name alone doesn't prove where the picture came from, so SMTO would refuse it again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's reply describes what is actually in the image or page, and this error doesn't appear.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Until this is solved, don't rely on any answer about that picture, because the model hasn't seen it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Vision tool rejected an image artifact because its registry entry has no pdf.render, screen.capture or screen.context producer with an operation ID, so its origin cannot be verified.

What this means

  • The artifact lacks the exact allowed pdf.render output, page and parent attachment provenance required by the Vision adapter. A filename or arbitrary artifact reference is insufficient. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The artifact lacks the exact allowed pdf.render output, page and parent attachment provenance required by the Vision adapter. A filename or arbitrary artifact reference is insufficient.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • In src/agent_runtime/skills/vision/tools.py artifact_image, the artifact's producer.producer_tool is not pdf.render, screen.capture or screen.context, or producer.operation_id is missing. Pass the context_id of an attached image, or run pdf.render on the attached PDF and pass the art_ IDs it returns; a filename or any other artifact ID is not accepted.
  • Render the selected pages through the authorized PDF tool and use its returned image artifact references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The image resolves to the producing PDF operation, page and authorized parent attachment.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
